BROKERDESK — AUTONOMOUS BROWSER ACCEPTANCE AFTER BATCH 2A

Read this task and the existing STABILITY-CHECKPOINT.md. Batch 1 and Batch 2A
have reported automated-test completion. Batch 2B and Batch 3 remain pending.
Do not repeat the full audit or implement those pending batches in this task.

The broker has no time to install/deploy software or manually exercise the UI.
Your job is to run the actual existing app and produce browser-level evidence,
not another static-inspection report. Use this supplied synthetic test pack.
All records are invented QA data, not customer documents.

1. ENVIRONMENT PREFLIGHT — DO THIS BEFORE WRITING MANY TESTS

Inspect only package scripts, current startup configuration, existing test tools,
and the checkpoint initially. Identify the current worktree/revision.

Try to start BOTH the real local backend and the real Vite/vinext application
in an isolated test environment, with a fresh disposable BROKERDESK_DATA_DIR,
separate test ports, and a fresh browser profile. Use the actual app startup
path so the PDF.js/SSR/Cloudflare/Vite boundary is exercised.

Use Playwright with Chromium or equivalent available real browser tooling.
Headless Chromium is acceptable. Do not substitute jsdom or source-string tests
for browser execution.

Do not reuse a service on the broker's normal ports. Do not read, modify, delete,
migrate, or back up the broker's actual customer database for these tests.
Bind test servers to loopback. Never expose them publicly.

If process/browser installation or startup is denied by permissions/EPERM:
- identify the exact command and policy/environment restriction;
- request the narrow approved execution/network permission once if supported;
- do not disable sandbox/security policy or repeatedly retry the same denial;
- use an already authorized cloud/Linux test environment only if it actually
  has this worktree and dependencies available;
- do not claim moving to cloud automatically transfers local files or secrets;
- if no executable environment is available, finish a runnable test entrypoint
  and record BROWSER BLOCKED, not PASSED. State the single minimum setup or
  approval needed. Do not ask the broker to install Docker/PaddleOCR.

2. FIXTURES AND ASSERTION SAFETY

Read expected/expected-results.json and README.md.
Use fixtures/ as real uploaded PDF/PNG bytes, not as JSON imports that bypass
PDF extraction.

These are deliberately synthetic simple layouts. Unsupported layouts may
legitimately require review. Record extraction quality separately from
workflow correctness. Do not force all values to pass by special-casing these
filenames, test people, VINs, or expected outputs in production code.

The ownership PDF has no embedded text. The mixed 12-page package has exactly
one image-only page (physical page 4). Other pages have selectable text.

The application in the mixed package is intentionally UNSIGNED. Do not grant
signed-document validity based on its document type or heading.

An expected JSON file is test ground truth, not an OCR response. Never write
its expected field values into application state to create a passing test.

3. SEPARATE OFFLINE WORKFLOW TESTS FROM LIVE OCR

Track test modes explicitly:
A. REAL_BROWSER_LOCAL: actual browser, backend, PDF.js, parsers and SQLite.
B. STUBBED_OCR: only the external provider response is a declared deterministic
   test stub; real rendering/request path/parsing/persistence still runs.
C. LIVE_OCR: real server-to-OCR.Space request using synthetic inputs only.

Offline runs must block accidental external cloud OCR, even if a real key is
present in .env.local. Prevent automatic upload OCR from leaking into offline
runs. Reuse existing test injection if available; any added adapter must be
explicitly test-only and never be a production default.

For LIVE_OCR, use the existing authorized server-side key, if available, without
printing, returning, committing, screenshotting, or placing it in browser code.
Use only the bundled synthetic input. Maximum THREE total outgoing OCR
requests for the entire live run, concurrency one, no automatic retries.
Count all retries/automatic requests in that budget.
Stop on authentication, quota or provider errors. No paid tier upgrade.
If a key/network is unavailable, mark LIVE_OCR BLOCKED; still run the other tests.
Do not upload any previous real client ownership/MVR/payment files to the cloud.

Provider configured/ONLINE is not proof of successful remote OCR. Record an
actual response status, character count and parsed-field result if a call runs.
No raw credentials in logs or test traces.

4. FIVE FOCUSED BROWSER SCENARIOS

SCENARIO A — Case lifecycle and persistence
- Start from an empty disposable database: no automatic case creation.
- Change Auto/HAB/Policy Change selector: still zero cases.
- Click + New case once: exactly one blank case, no sample insurance facts.
- Create a second case; select/edit the older one: list order stays stable.
- Preserve a note/manual entry across page reload and a REAL backend restart
  against the same disposable data directory.
- Delete the final test case: empty page, no replacement Auto case.
Use valid configured completion conditions if testing KEYED/INCOMPLETE;
do not bypass real blockers to make the status test pass.

SCENARIO B — Searchable PDF, two drivers, report boundaries
- Through UI uploads, use 01, 03 and 04 fixture PDFs in a fresh Auto case.
- Use explicit test-driver creation/association through normal UI if needed;
  name-only unassigned data should not silently target driver one.
- Verify different MVR reply dates/demerits/convictions do not cross subjects.
- Verify each three-page DASH stays together, but report A and B stay separate.
- Verify the old claim remains visible despite zero recent claims in summary.
- Verify third-party role and unknown first-party fault remain distinct.
- Verify all claim views use the intended effective date, not a hardcoded date.
- Searchable PDFs require zero external OCR calls.
If UI prevents an association needed for safe review, record that usability gap.

SCENARIO C — Actual PDF worker, scan and mixed package
- Open 02_ownership_scan.pdf and exercise real browser rendering.
- In STUBBED_OCR mode, return declared synthetic provider test data only at the
  provider boundary; do not bypass rendering, ingestion or reconciliation.
- In LIVE_OCR mode, use this scan only within the total request budget.
- Upload 05_mixed_auto_package.pdf: analyze real pages, preserve original bytes,
  and verify original-page provenance and separate MVR/DASH subjects.
- Do not send the full 12-page PDF to cloud OCR. Only its scan page is eligible.
- Parser-only refresh/reload/case switch makes zero additional OCR calls.
- Failures appear on the document card, not a full-page runtime crash.

SCENARIO D — Active evidence, manual sections and rename
- In a test case, manually classify/edit a logical section.
- Reparse: manual type/subject association remains intact.
- Delete that section: its automatic facts stop contributing; siblings and
  the physical source remain. Preserve manual decisions with withdrawn-source
  review status where appropriate.
- Rename a combined package via UI: originalFilename remains, current file
  exists with accepted name, logical references still open after restart.
Do not infer document validity from FOUND or from successful extraction.

SCENARIO E — UI errors, controls and known pending findings
- Capture pageerror, unhandled errors, worker failures, and failed local requests.
- Exercise desktop and one narrow viewport; make a final bottom-control
  screenshot. Check buttons are reachable and the giant empty region is absent.
- File-picker automation and DOM drag/drop are distinct tests; do not claim
  Windows Explorer-native drag validation from DOM event simulation.
- Use 06/07 only to record current Batch 2B/3 baseline observations, NOT to mark
  pending requirements complete or expand this task into those fixes.

5. REPRODUCIBLE OUTPUT AND TOKEN CONTROL

Use the existing test framework. Prefer one named repeatable command, one worker,
retries=0, and a bounded run. Run failed-scenario retests after a justified small
fix, not the entire historic suite repeatedly.

Do not change business rules, thresholds, test assertions or fixture truth
merely to turn failures green. Clear small defects in previously completed work
may be fixed with focused tests. New large defects go into the checkpoint.

Keep full logs in files, not the chat. Produce:
- browser-test-report.md: scenario results and exact commands/revision;
- machine-readable pass/fail/blocked/skipped results;
- selected screenshots of real app states;
- a retained failure trace, if supported;
- OCR call counts by real/stubbed mode;
- a precise note on test-server restart vs OS restart;
- updated STABILITY-CHECKPOINT.md, keeping Batch 2B/3 pending.

Final response maximum 400 words. Explicitly distinguish:
ACTUAL_BROWSER_PASS / FAILED / BLOCKED / NOT_RUN,
STUBBED_OCR versus LIVE_OCR,
and synthetic-fixture testing versus real-client-document accuracy.

Do not claim Windows production usability from a Linux-only test.
Do not start PaddleOCR, cloud product deployment, multi-user auth, or new phases.
Then STOP.
